title: Tech Trends 2022
notes: 13th annual edition (archive page: 'Deloitte’s 13th annual Tech Trends report explores seven trends'). Six trend chapters (entries 1-6) and a seventh chapter, 'Field notes from the future', on three emerging technologies with a next-decade horizon (entries 7-9). This edition has no edition-level 18-to-24-month statement; horizons are recorded only where a chapter states one. Letter from the editors: 'Enterprises once viewed the types of initiatives we spotlight as projects that would play out over the next five to 10 years. The reality? These trends need to be tackled today.' Published month not stated in the PDF.

entries.label: Data-sharing made easy
entries.quote: During the next 18 to 24 months, we expect to see more organizations explore opportunities to create seamless, secure data-sharing capabilities that can help them monetize their own information assets
entries.subject: Data sharing and privacy-preserving computation
entries.note: Same chapter: 'within the next 18 to 24 months, privacy-preserving computing will offer a broad range of use cases and opportunities'.

entries.label: Cloud goes vertical
entries.quote: Over the next 18 to 24 months, we expect to see a growing number of organizations across market sectors begin exploring ways that industry clouds can help them meet unique vertical needs.
entries.subject: Industry (vertical) clouds

entries.label: Blockchain: Ready for business
entries.quote: Distributed ledger technologies are changing the nature of doing business and helping companies reimagine how they manage tangible and digital assets
entries.subject: Blockchain and distributed ledgers
entries.note: Chapter subtitle. No horizon stated in the chapter. Executive summary: blockchain and DLT platforms 'have crossed the disillusionment trough of the hype cycle and are well on their way to driving real productivity'.

entries.label: IT, disrupt thyself: Automating at scale
entries.quote: Future-forward IT organizations are modernizing the “IT back office” to a proactive model of self-service and engineered automation
entries.subject: IT automation (self-service, engineered automation)
entries.note: Chapter subtitle. No horizon stated in the chapter.

entries.label: Cyber AI: Real defense
entries.quote: Nation-states are already entering this territory, and we may see more from private cybercrime actors in the next 18 to 24 months.
entries.subject: AI in cybersecurity
entries.note: 'This territory' is attackers developing AI to complicate their attacks.

entries.label: The tech stack goes physical
entries.quote: CIOs increasingly need to manage physical technology stacks
entries.subject: Physical technology stack (smart devices, robots, edge)
entries.note: Chapter subtitle. No horizon stated in the chapter.

entries.label: Quantum and then some
entries.quote: Quantum research goes commercial in the next decade.
entries.subject: Quantum technologies (computing, sensing, communications)
entries.note: Chapter: 'Quantum technologies, which are poised to transform computing, sensing, and communications within the next decade'.

entries.label: Exponential intelligence: Once more, with feeling
entries.quote: During the next decade, affective computing will continue to morph and grow as innovators train machines, through next-generation deep learning techniques, to both recognize and emulate human traits
entries.subject: Affective computing (emotion AI)

entries.label: Ambient experience: Life beyond the glass
entries.quote: During the next decade, ambient computing—a catchall term for a growing field of technologies and techniques that make digital reality available to users anytime and anywhere—will become our standard modality
entries.subject: Ambient computing
